missing_families.why: This is the best-shaped gap. Each sale is small ($1-4 per face or data field). Buyers come to a store on the device or its companion app. The product is code (Monkey C, Watch Face Format XML, Zepp JS) plus drawn vector graphics, not generative images, so the AI bans that killed media venues (groups/licensing-ip.md:133-136; itch.io in this sweep) are less likely to reach it. The colony already has a home-turf asset: mcp-il-tools ships a hebrew_date tool (products/mcp-il-tools/src/server.ts:86), fixed and ICU-checked for 1900-2100 in every timezone (logs/CHANNEL_LOOP.md:110). That makes a Hebrew-date, zmanim or Shabbat-entry face or complication for Israeli and Jewish watch owners a distinct audience under constraint 6. It must be counted by function, not by skin: colour variants are substitution (BOARD-LOOP BUILD-3). One seller account can carry several functionally distinct faces. Repo coverage: a grep on 28.9 for Garmin, Connect IQ, Wear OS, watch face, Facer, Zepp and Fitbit gives 0 hits. Samsung appears only as a Playgama partner (research/breadth/scouts/html5-games.json:104). Google Play faces are already excluded by the $25 fee (INCOME_PLAN.he.md §4; ₪0 rule). Every gate is UNKNOWN, grade none: the paid-app mechanism and payee countries (Garmin, Samsung commercial seller), any camera step, an upload API (Samsung's Galaxy Store Developer API / Content Publish API is known here only from memory), the AI rules, whether discovery ranks on prior sales, and the price floor (free Hebrew-calendar faces may exist; the AMO verifier found free Hebrew-date add-ons). Estimate: ₪0 low; there is no base rate in the repo, so the high end is not estimable. Kill shape: a registration fee, a selfie, or a per-face owner click.

missing_families.why: This family runs on long-tail, exact-title demand: each song × instrument × level cell is a separate search with few competitors, at $1-6 a copy. That is the one discovery shape that might not rank purely on prior success (the four-platform law, REJECTED.md:1105-1121). It is UNKNOWN until one cell's occupancy is measured. Notation is code (MusicXML/LilyPond), with machine-checkable correctness: range, key and playability limits. ArrangeMe (Hal Leonard) licenses copyrighted songs to the arranger (grade none, from memory), and that is where honest value lies. Public-domain engravings fail the constitution, because IMSLP and MuseScore give them away (REJECTED.md:1240, 'never sell what is already free'). Repo coverage: 0 hits for ArrangeMe, Musicnotes, MuseScore or 'sheet music' (grep 28.9). licensing-ip swept audio only (scouts/licensing-ip--music-sfx.md), and the rejection of AI music on streaming (groups/licensing-ip.md:176) is about audio, not notation. Stated risks: (1) upload is probably a web form per title with no API. That is the same kill shape as the Adobe portal (REJECTED.md:1006-1010) and the signed-in forms (REJECTED.md:1169, 1172), unless a bulk or API channel renders. (2) The AI policy is UNKNOWN. (3) An arrangement no musician checked may be AI slop, so it must be declared, and the catalogue limited to mechanically verifiable forms. (4) Payout rail, Israel and camera are UNKNOWN; a W-8BEN is a one-time owner step. Estimate ₪0 low; the high end is not estimable (no base rate).

Sheet Music Plus SMP Press (https://www.sheetmusicplus.com: the publish and terms pages). Musicnotes Marketplace (https://www.musicnotes.com). MyMusicSheet (https://www.mymusicsheet.com). Score Exchange (https://www.scoreexchange.com). First check: whether any of them documents a bulk or API upload. Without one, KILL on the Adobe precedent.

missing_families.why: These are venues where AI authorship is the declared product: paid prompt markets, and model or workflow markets with per-use creator rewards. There, the AI-honesty gate that killed itch.io (this sweep), Shutterstock, Pond5, Envato and TurboSquid (groups/licensing-ip.md:133-136) cannot fire, and tickets are $2-10 or per-use rewards. Repo coverage: 0 hits for PromptBase, Civitai, OpenArt or Tensor.art (grep 28.9). agent-markets--skill-marketplaces.md covered Claude plugins and skills (no payment rail), not paid prompt or model markets. The weaknesses, stated up front: (1) the price floor is near zero, because prompts are shared free (REJECTED.md:1240); (2) training models costs GPU money (₪0 rule) unless free on-platform credits suffice; (3) Civitai's likeness and NSFW moderation history is a brand risk; (4) payouts: PromptBase uses Stripe Connect (Israel only through cross-border; the Stripe question is open at REJECTED.md:1402-1426), and Civitai's cash-out rail is UNKNOWN. Civitai's code is open (github.com/civitai/civitai), so its cash-out, KYC and country rules can be read at github grade for free. Considered and deliberately NOT proposed: game-mod revenue-share platforms. I read three Modrinth files at github grade today. The API can create projects (modrinth/code apps/labrinth/src/routes/v3/project_creation.rs: POST /project, scope PROJECT_CREATE, new projects go to status Processing for review). Payouts go by PayPal, Venmo, Tremendous, MuralPay or USDC on Polygon, behind an Avalara tax-form and TIN gate (routes/v3/payouts.rs). But the rules (apps/frontend/src/pages/legal/rules.vue) say 'Projects cannot be entirely or primarily comprised of content created or derived from generative AI output', and they ban AI images on project pages. That FAILs the AI gate for this colony, as itch.io did. CurseForge Rewards and Nexus Mods Donation Points were not read.
missing_families.seeds: PromptBase (https://promptbase.com/sell ; https://promptbase.com/faq ; https://promptbase.com/terms). Civitai Creator Program (https://github.com/civitai/civitai: grep it for cash-out/Tipalti/KYC/country; live terms at https://civitai.com/content/tos). OpenArt workflow creators (https://openart.ai). If the family is ever reopened on mods: CurseForge authors rewards (https://support.curseforge.com) and Nexus Mods Donation Points (https://www.nexusmods.com/about/donationpoints), AI rules first.

contradictions_with_repo: APIFY INSTRUMENT (the most important). REJECTED.md:820 says free publishing 'needs no KYC… and it starts the one clock — History of success'. BOARD-LOOP.md:89-92 and :210 defer Apify KYC until ≥50 stranger users. Apify's OpenAPI spec (github, confirmed today) hides Actors of developers without KYC from default Store-API search. That makes the design circular: KYC waits on users, and agent/API visibility waits on KYC. It affects BOARD-LOOP rank 1, the constraint-7 instrument, not just the scout's fleet (which the verifier killed). It needs a Fable ruling on whether the 30-day stranger count is valid without KYC.

WHOP RAIL. REJECTED.md:1068-1069 says Whop payout 'needs a one-time ID upload' and records the rail 'as reusable by any line selling to a US audience'. The storefront-rails scout (github, Whop's official SDK) says a 'Photo of the person's face… Always required, with every document type'. The REJECTED.md entry should be re-recorded as camera-gated (KILL-4 shape), not reusable.

GUMROAD FEE ARITHMETIC. src/revenue/rails.ts:81 gives '12.9% + $0.80, plus 2.9% + $0.30… about 22% on a $9 product'. Those components sum to about 28.0% at $9: (1.161+0.80+0.261+0.30)/9. About 22% holds only near $19. REJECTED.md:1382 ('17–22% at small tickets') and rails.ts:352 repeat the understatement. The Firefox verifier's 28-38% agrees with the arithmetic. Every Gumroad-rail estimate at $5-9 tickets is overstated.
